_comment: Ingredients matched here are discrete/countable items where a fractional scaled amount isn't practical to use. 'keyword' is matched as a whole word (plural allowed) against the ingredient part of each parsed name (before the first comma), so 'egg' catches 'large eggs', 'egg whites' and 'egg yolks' but not 'eggplant' or a crust 'brushed with egg wash'. Add entries as you run into more of these.

ingredients.note: Eggs don't divide cleanly. If the scaled amount isn't a whole number, round to the nearest whole egg, or whisk one egg and measure out a partial amount by volume (about 3 tablespoons per large egg) if precision matters.
Whole crackers/sheets don't split cleanly. Round to the nearest whole cracker, extra crumbs from a slightly-over amount are rarely a problem.
A pie crust isn't a divisible quantity. Scaling likely means you need a different pan size or an extra crust, not a fractional one.
Gelatin sheets are discrete units. Round to the nearest whole sheet, sheet gelatin has some flex in practice.
